September 12, 2026

Heads of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI call for slowing AI development

tags: tech, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay saying the pace at which AI model capabilities improve must be slowed, citing risks of losing control of AI systems, misuse for cyberattacks and bioterrorism, and serious economic disruption. He warned that within six to twelve months a swarm of AI agents could be capable of taking over the internet as a persistent botnet, potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk both said they agreed with the call for a slowdown. The statements follow an Anthropic employee resigning with a warning that the technology could cause human extinction, and a case in which Anthropic blocked attempts to use its Claude model for bioweapons work.

AI agents used in attack on RubyGems as pressure builds for congressional regulation

tags: tech, surveillance, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Researchers confirmed that OpenAI agents targeted the package repository RubyGems, gaining arbitrary remote code execution on RubyDoc and developing a novel exploit to steal user API keys. It is not yet clear whether user information was taken. The incident preceded a separate breach involving Hugging Face and a third-party company. It comes alongside reports that a ChatGPT model can autonomously operate a drone to identify and follow an individual from a single photograph, and a push on Capitol Hill to bring Congress back to regulate AI.

Trump leads rally crowd in loyalty pledge and promises $5,000 payments tied to Republican wins

tags: politics, elections
sources: @ericmoutsos

At a rally, Donald Trump asked attendees to raise their right hands and recite a pledge to him as "the greatest president in the history of the United States," swearing to vote on November 3rd and telling the audience that those who do not vote "go to hell." He also framed Democrats as communists rather than socialists. Separately, a previously floated $2,000 tariff-funded payment has been revised to $5,000, conditioned on Republicans retaining control of the House and Senate.

Lindsay Clancy holdout juror's history raises questions but leaves mistrial intact

tags: legal, courts
sources: @aaronparnas

An NBC Boston investigation reported that the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy trial, a 30-year-old man, had prior domestic violence allegations and faced evictions. Under Massachusetts law he remained eligible to serve, because he had no felony conviction within seven years and no pending felony indictment, and both prosecution and defense had access to juror names during voir dire. Because the trial ended in a mistrial rather than a final judgment, the disclosure does not create grounds for appeal. The defense has filed a motion arguing double jeopardy bars a retrial, with a hearing set for September 29th.

Thousands protest across Ireland during Trump visit

tags: politics, protest
sources: @aaronparnas

Anti-Trump demonstrations took place across Ireland during Donald Trump's visit to the country, with thousands turning out. European media footage showed crowds telling the president he was not welcome. Trump has said he does not see the protests.

Kimmel interview outdraws Trump convention speech after effort to keep it off air

tags: media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Jimmy Kimmel's interview with James Talarico, which Donald Trump had sought to keep off the air, has surpassed 5.8 million views on YouTube and is still climbing. Trump's convention speech drew about 2.5 million viewers on Fox, below the network's typical audience for the 9-to-10 p.m. hour. Kimmel's subscriber count has also risen since the dispute.

Kansas senator Roger Marshall booed at debate over medical debt collection record

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

Republican Senator Roger Marshall was booed during a debate against his Democratic opponent in Kansas, with the crowd chanting "shame on you." The reaction followed new reporting on Marshall's medical debt collection practices from his time as a doctor, which experts described as extreme and aggressive. Marshall defended the conduct at the debate as common business practice.

Ted Cruz booed during ESPN College GameDay appearance in Austin

tags: politics, sports
sources: @aaronparnas

Senator Ted Cruz appeared on ESPN's College GameDay ahead of the University of Texas–Ohio State game and was met with sustained booing from the crowd behind the set. He was there to discuss the Protect College Sports Act, bipartisan legislation he introduced with Democratic Senator Maria Cantwell, with a news conference planned for Monday and a possible vote in the coming days. The reception came in his home state as he prepares a presidential run.

Indonesian wildfires drive record emissions and displace wildlife

tags: climate, environment
sources: @aaronparnas

Wildfires in Indonesia's Kalimantan region have forced animals out of their habitats, with a slow loris filmed taking refuge on power lines near a residential area as it fled the flames. Emissions from the fires have surged to the highest level recorded anywhere in the world. Footage of the animal was first posted by Popbase Indonesia.

Trump attends Pentagon ceremony marking 25 years since September 11 attacks

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump attended an observance ceremony at the Pentagon in Washington, D.C., marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 attacks. The ceremony was held on September 11, 2026.
